target.title: fix(ssrf): block loopback addresses for trusted hostname origins
target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where ssrf dns rebinding/private network check bypass (pr #100835).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
Matching an allowed origin sets `skipPrivateNetworkChecks` to `true`, which bypasses `assertAllowedResolvedAddressesOrThrow` in favor of `assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow`. The latter only checks for link-local and cloud metadata IPs, leaving loopback (`127.0.0.1`) and RFC 1918 private IPs completely allowed. This exposes the gateway to DNS rebinding attacks targeting localhost services.

Affected location: `[src/infra/net/ssrf.ts](file://src/infra/net/ssrf.ts#L413-L421) (compiled as `dist/ssrf-DmSIVBht.js`)`

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to resolve the logic discrepancy.

**Solution Overview:**
Add a loopback check in `assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow` to block connections to local hosts even for trusted hostnames.
  ```javascript
  function assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow(results) {
      for (const entry of results) {
          if (isLinkLocalIpAddress(entry.address) || isCloudMetadataIpAddress(entry.address) || isLoopbackIpAddress(entry.address)) {
              throw new SsrFBlockedError(BLOCKED_RESOLVED_IP_MESSAGE);
          }
      }
  }
  ```

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that: Hostnames configured in `allowedOrigins` (and mapped to `allowedHostnames`) should not bypass loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`) or private IP checks unless `allowPrivateNetwork` is explicitly allowed by policy, preventing DNS rebinding attacks.

## Evidence

<!-- Unit tests and validation logs -->

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite
- Reproduction tests run successfully.

### Real Behavior Proof

#### Before (Failing Reproduction):
```text
AssertionError: promise resolved "{ …(3) }" instead of rejecting

- Expected
+ Received

- Error {
-   "message": "rejected promise",
+ {
+   "addresses": [
+     "127.0.0.1",
+   ],
+   "hostname": "lan-llm.corp.internal",
+   "lookup": [Function anonymous],
  }

 ❯ src/plugin-sdk/ssrf-policy.test.ts:472:6
    470|         lookupFn: createLookupFn([{ address: "127.0.0.1", family: 4 }]…
    471|       }),
    472|     ).rejects.toThrow(SsrFBlockedError);
       |      ^
    473|   });
```
